answer: Whether an agent books a berth at a jetty, buys a vine, or rents a lantern, its influence in the marketplace is proportional to tokens locked in a staking contract, never to its number of accounts. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities still yields only 100 tokens of voting weight. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens, paying acquisition costs and forgoing other uses of that capital.
